terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A parked vehicle prop: an exterior shell with no interior geometry, since a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside and the glazing is authored as a tinted, mostly opaque pane. The wheels are the mechanisms: each is a named pivot on its axle. Nothing else moves and nothing attaches, so there are no sockets. A Bangkok tuk-tuk. The plate shows a glossy green scooter nose with a yellow band and a single headlamp, a raked leg shield with handlebars above it, a checker-plate floor, a green cabin tub with a yellow belt stripe and chrome rails, a dark green vinyl bench with a back, a flat green canopy on chrome pillars with a chrome edge rail, a chrome basket on the tail, one front wheel and two rear wheels.

reasoning: The identity is the three-part layout read straight off the proxy: a scooter nose (leg shield, single front wheel, bars) at 0.00-0.27 L, an open floor, and a rear cabin tub with a bench under a flat green canopy on chrome pillars over 0.21-0.79 L.
Two materials: the paint (green tub, nose, canopy, yellow band and stripe as vertex colours) and a white vertex-coloured trim (chrome rails and basket, vinyl bench, checker floor, lamps, tyres).
One repetition system: three wheels off one lathe, each a named pivot on its axle.
Action readiness is the wheels: three hinge pivots, convex collider, not breakable. Steering is not articulated.

specDepthDecision.rationale: An auto rickshaw is legible by its openness -- no doors, no side glass, a canopy on four thin pillars -- so the cabin is a tub extrusion open to the front with the canopy a separate slab on chrome tubes, and the turntable sees the backdrop through it from every side: that is the vehicle, not a hole in the model.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The cabin is open-sided and the turntable gate's enclosed-background signal fires on the backdrop seen through it from every azimuth (290 x 197 px from the sides). That is real open air; --allow-holes is set on the _holecc measurement.
The canopy is a flat slab with rounded plan corners rather than the plate's domed shell; the dome is below the resolvable band at prop distance and would cost a lathe.
The tail panel behind the basket is built to type.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 1.40 x 1.95 x 2.90 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus one named pivot per wheel (3); zero sockets; convex collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

silhouette.description: Front wheel 0.52 m at z +1.17, rear wheels at z -0.67 on a 1.12 m track; a fender arc over the front wheel; leg shield 0.34-1.02 m at z 0.80-1.06 with the bars at 1.16 m; floor at 0.21 m; cabin tub 0.30-0.62 m from z 0.02 to -1.45; bench at 0.72 m with a back to 1.22 m; canopy 1.80-1.95 m from z 0.86 to -1.32 on pillars at z 0.02 and -1.10; basket to z -1.47.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -0.67..+0.67 at the cabin and canopy; y 0.00 to 1.95 at the canopy; z -1.52..+1.43 basket to fender, +Z forward. The Meshy proxy normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.662 : 0.449, i.e. 2.90 x 1.92 x 1.30 m at the declared length -- within 2 percent of the registry on height and 7 on width -- so the declaration stands and every station is a proxy fraction.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.662 : 0.449 and agrees with the registry. Its occupancy map (scratch/tuk-tuk/_ev/occupancy.txt) reads the canopy at 0.96-1.00 H over 0.21-0.79 L, the rear pillar at 0.79-0.85 L, bars at 0.60 H over 0.20-0.27 L, the front wheel 0.00-0.30 H over 0.00-0.17 L, rear wheels over 0.65-0.82 L, the floor at 0.14-0.16 H, and the cabin tub to 0.64 H over 0.58-0.88 L -- and those fractions at the declared metres are what is built.

evidence: Green measured on viewEvidence region-green (cabin side, PBR confidence 0.764) at #2d6542 and yellow on region-yellow (nose, 0.798) at #e1ad10; both as vertex colours on one white material, so the two-tone costs an attribute, not a material.
Textureless as DECLARED: gloss enamel; a faint dust multiplier canvas is bound after construction.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 1.34 x 1.95 x 2.95 m against a declared 1.40 x 1.95 x 2.90; the proxy agrees with the declaration (1 : 0.662 : 0.449) and every station is its fraction.
featureReviews.notes: Canopy 0.21-0.79 L, rear pillar at 0.79-0.85 L, bars 0.60 H, front wheel 0.00-0.17 L, rear wheels 0.65-0.82 L -- all off the occupancy map. THE PROXY'S UPPER BANDS ARE NOT EVIDENCE HERE and were not chased: the ten-band table reads reference depth 1.008 at band 6, 0.302 at band 7, 0.348 at band 8 and 0.878 at band 9, i.e. a machine that necks to 0.59 m front-to-back between two full-length sections and flares out again. No tuk-tuk does that; it is Meshy losing four thin canopy pillars, which is the documented failure mode on separated thin members, and bands 7-8 are exactly the open cabin where the only geometry IS those pillars. The band table decided the spirit house in this same session and is the right instrument when the proxy is coherent -- it is not coherent here, and the plate comparison is.

featureReviews.evidence: Three instanced wheels, tyre #3a3025 with a chrome hub at 40% of the tyre radius, measured off the plate (hub 84 px across a 212 px tyre). One lathe, three instances.
featureReviews.notes: The wheels rendered as PALE GREY PLATES and two separate things were behind it. `wheelGeo` interpolates the rim colour outward from rRim to the tread, so the whole sidewall is a gradient from hub tone to tyre tone -- shrinking the rim only made the pale gradient wider. `rimBand` (default unchanged, so every other vehicle is byte-identical: verified against the shipped songthaew bundle at max |diff| 0 over position AND colour) stops the chrome at the hub cap. And the old tyre #4d4b46 sat INSIDE the turntable gate's backdrop test at luma 75 (|d| 17 <= 24) and saturation 0.09 (<= 0.16); it is held on CHROMA now at luma 52, saturation 0.36.

featureReviews.evidence: Green side walls rising 0.70 -> 0.94 toward the tail, a solid rear wall behind the bench, a pair of 45 mm GREEN rear canopy pillars, a thin chrome front pillar, belt and edge rails, bench and back, driver's saddle and footboard, chrome basket on the tail.
featureReviews.notes: The first build carried the canopy on four thin chrome sticks over a 0.32 m tub and read as a frame with no body: the plate's cabin is enclosed to above the seat cushion and its REAR pillars are green bodywork, not chrome. Two further faults came out of the 270 view rather than any gate -- the tub bottom sat at 0.30 while the checker floor was at 0.17, so a 1.24 x 1.50 m plate hung out below the bodywork on both sides and the prop read as a scooter standing on a pallet; and the body stopped at z 0.02 leaving a gap to the nose that the driver's footboard floated in. The tub now runs from z 0.74 to the tail with its bottom at 0.15. The turntable's enclosed backdrop is the open cabin, allowed on the _holecc measurement.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 3,244/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries, one 256 px canvas at 0.3 MB, factory 108 ms. Turntable: enclosed background is the open cabin, allowed on measurement.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components and one repetition system: 3 of 4.

materials.note: paint and a white vertex-coloured trim: 2 of 3; green and yellow are vertex colours.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 2,700 of 4,000: an 18-segment wheel lathe (three instances), 8-segment tubes, thin extrusions.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Side-profile extrusions for nose, fender, tub, back wall and canopy; polyline tubes for every chrome part; one wheel lathe; boxes for bench, floor, lamps.
One InstancedMesh carries all three wheels. No per-instance colour.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Every material is declared textureless. One 256 px dust canvas on the paint. 0.3 MB of texture VRAM, factory 108 ms.

risks.description: The turntable gate flags the backdrop through the open cabin at every azimuth.
risks.mitigation: Real open air; --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement.

risks.mitigation: Below the resolvable band at prop distance; recorded as an assumption.
